1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 {Hopefully, we will one day see more Evan's
Gambits in the World Championship.} 4... Bxb4 {Whether or not, players in the
1800s felt honor-bound to accept the sacrifice, Steinitz was a man of principal
and was determined to accept and refute such gambits.} 5. c3 Ba5 6. O-O d6 7. d4
Bg4 8. Bb5 exd4 9. cxd4 Bd7 $2 {Steinitz makes a clear concession. Obviously,
retreating the bishop that just advanced to g4 cannot be correct.} (9... Ne7
{Simply developing and readying to castle is right. d5 can be met by a6.}) 10.
Bb2 Nce7 11. Bxd7+ Qxd7 12. Na3 {The knight goes to the side of the board with
the purpose of returning to a central location on c4, hitting the a5-knight and
supporting e5.} 12... Nh6 (12... Nf6 13. Nc4 Bb6 14. a4 $16 {creates strong
pressure and a nice advantage for White, but it definitely better to have the
knight on f6 than h6.}) 13. Nc4 Bb6 14. a4 c6 15. e5 d5 $2 {A fatal decision. The
knight on d6 and the loss of the right to castle cannot be survived.} (15...
dxe5 {Black must exchange the pawn and try to hold.} 16. dxe5 Qxd1 17. Raxd1 O-O
18. Ba3 c5 19. Rd7 Nc6 20. Rxb7 {White has a better structure and better pieces
and a good advantage, but Black is not lost.}) 16. Nd6+ Kf8 17. Ba3 {directing
the bishop at the king.} 17... Kg8 18. Rb1 Nhf5 19. Nxf7 $3 {The tactical
Steinitz finds a delightful winning path. One knight is surrendered, but the
other will be a monster on e5.} 19... Kxf7 20. e6+ $1 Kxe6 (20... Qxe6 21. Ng5+ $18
{is a nice royal fork.}) 21. Ne5 Qc8 22. Re1 {Black's king is in the line of the
fire, and there's no good way to evacuate it.} 22... Kf6 23. Qh5 {Threatening
Ng4# and Qf7+.} 23... g6 (23... Rf8 24. Ng4#) (23... Ng6 24. Bc1 Nxe5 25. Bg5+
Ke6 26. Rxe5+ Kd6 27. Bf4 {Arranges the threat of another discovered check (and
threatens f5), and forces checkmate in 9 at most according to the engine.}) 24.
Bxe7+ Kxe7 (24... Nxe7 {This loses, often spectacularly, but possibly, it would
have been more effective to resist this way as Chigorin would need to find some
nice moves.} 25. Qh4+ g5 26. Ng4+ Kf7 27. Rxe7+ $3 {Prettiest and most
effective.} 27... Kxe7 28. Qxg5+ Kd7 29. Nf6+ Kd6 30. Qe5#) 25. Nxg6+ Kf6 26.
Nxh8 Bxd4 {A clever try. Picking off d4, and hoping to win the trapped knight on
the next move.} (26... Qxh8 {Immediately capturing the knight keeps Black ahead
on material, but White's heavy pieces overwhelm Black in all lines.} 27. Re5 Nd6
(27... Nxd4 28. Qg5+ Kf7 29. Qe7+ Kg6 30. Rg5+ Kh6 31. Rg4 $18) 28. Rb3 $18) 27.
Rb3 Qd7 28. Rf3 Rxh8 {Black has the material advantage, but...} 29. g4 {The
knight now falls.} 29... Rg8 30. Qh6+ Rg6 (30... Kf7 31. Rxf5+ $4 {It's always
possible to go wrong.} (31. Qxh7+ $1 Rg7 32. Rxf5+ Qxf5 33. Qxf5+ $18) 31... Qxf5
$19) 31. Rxf5+ $1 {Chigorin forces resignation with yet another little tactic.}
(31. Rxf5+ Qxf5 32. Qf8+ {wins the queen due to the skewer and mates soon
after.}) 1-0
